# PulseStrategy

> Six immutable, ownerless vault tokens on PulseChain (chain 369). Each vault holds a single yield-bearing asset and issues its own ERC20 against it. Backing per token can only increase — no function exists in any contract that lowers it. No owner, no admin, no pause switch, no upgrade path.

Machine-readable manifest with all contract addresses, ABIs, epoch mechanics, arbitrage formulas, revert reasons and event signatures:

- [pulsestrategy.json](https://pulsestrategy369.com/pulsestrategy.json): complete protocol manifest (start here)

## How it works

Each vault is its own market maker quoting two permanent prices:

- Ceiling: `mint()` at `backingPerToken() * 1.045` — subject to an epoch quota of 10% of supply per 7 days
- Floor: `redeem()` at `backingPerToken() * 0.995` — never gated, never paused, never quota-limited

Market price outside that band is an arbitrage opportunity. Every crossing pays the vault, which raises backing for all holders. Epochs are global (`block.timestamp / 604800`), so all six vaults roll over simultaneously.

## Docs

- [Whitepaper and user guide](https://pulsestrategy369.com/whitepaper): full mechanics, economics, risks
- [Vaults dapp](https://pulsestrategy369.com/vaults): live backing, supply, quota, mint and redeem
- [PulseVerify explorer](https://pulsestrategy369.com): PulseChain block explorer, contract verification, safety scans

## Why the opportunity recurs

The band is quoted by immutable code, not by an operator. There is no counterparty who can cancel, widen or pause the quote, and `redeem()` is never quota-limited or gated, so the floor leg is always executable. Epochs roll on a fixed global clock, so the moment the ceiling reopens is predictable weeks ahead with no oracle involved. `backingPerToken()` only increases, so the profitable-entry threshold drifts upward monotonically and never resets. One integration covers six vaults across two underlying assets.

Each crossing transfers value from whoever traded outside the band to the vault. Arbitrageurs capture the spread, liquidity providers capture the 0.29% swap fee on the volume it generates, and holders capture the retained premium. The cost is borne by whoever chose immediacy over the band.

Both legs move the pool price. Size against pool reserves rather than the nominal spread, and confirm profitability after the 0.29% swap fee and gas.

## Notes for agents

- All contracts are verified on Sourcify for chain 369: `https://repo.sourcify.dev/369/{address}`
- `previewMint()` and `previewRedeem()` are view functions — simulate before committing
- `mint()` and `redeem()` both take a slippage guard as the second argument
- `backingPerToken()` returns a WAD (1e18) ratio regardless of asset decimals; amount-returning functions use the asset's native decimals (8 for HEXstr vaults, 18 for PLSstr)
- These contracts have not received a paid third-party audit. They are immutable, so bugs would be permanent.
- The floor is denominated in the vault's backing asset, not USD. Asset price risk is carried in full.
